title: A replayed campaign can still diverge on a slow host, because three timers decide control flow and no recording holds the clock
foundBy: session agent, maintainer of this repository, after repeated replays of one recorded campaign on a shared host
details:
**What this is.** SAC-033 asks for `--record` and `--replay`, and lists what a replay has to hold still. Its fifth point says that the wait must not be shortened. It does not say that a replay has to take the clock out altogether. A cassette fixes what the models say. It cannot fix how long an agent's real work takes, such as a package install, and three timers in this harness turn elapsed time into control flow.

1. **The stall prod.** A member with an open dispatch and no activity for `StallSeconds`, 180 by default for a worker, is prodded with a new input. That is a model request the cassette never held, so the proxy counts a miss.
2. **The wait chunk.** `wait` returns when its chunk elapses, 240 seconds by default, whether or not a reply arrived. The proxy tolerates the changed tool result. The recorded orchestrator then carries on as if the work had arrived. The conversation replays without a miss, and the delivery is wrong.
3. **The readback bound.** A first turn that takes more than 15 minutes fails the create. No flag raises it.

**What was measured.** Thirteen replays of one recording of a three member campaign ran on a shared host, up to three at once. All served the same calls in the same order and gave the same commit ids, and no member was prodded. In one run the largest gap between two model calls of one member was a little over 150 seconds. Which timer that gap ran against was not established. If it was a `wait`, a host about one and a half times slower crosses the chunk.

**What is asked for.** A way to run a campaign in which none of the three timers can change control flow. `wait` returns only on a real reply, or on a bound long enough to mean failure. A stalled member is reported and not prodded. The readback bound is raised or lifted. It belongs to the `--replay` of SAC-033. It is useful before that flag exists, as a setting that a wrapper script can apply. A replay that does hit a bound has to fail and name the timer, and must never carry on.

**How to reproduce.** Replay a recorded campaign with the members' CPU limited until a worker's package install takes more than 240 seconds. The second failure above appears with no miss at all.
